Q: Determine how to identify this runtime error message A:

//@version=5

indicator("Demand Zone – Explosive Green + Base (Final)", overlay=true)

// =====================

// STEP 1: CMP (Auto / Manual)

// =====================

useAutoCMP = input.bool(true, "Use Auto CMP (Close Price)")

manualCMP = input.float(2450.0, "Manual CMP")

cmp = useAutoCMP ? close : manualCMP

// CMP Horizontal Line

var line cmpLine = na

if na(cmpLine)

cmpLine := line.new(bar_index, cmp, bar_index + 1, cmp, extend=extend.right, color=color.yellow, width=2)

else

line.set_y1(cmpLine, cmp)

line.set_y2(cmpLine, cmp)

// =====================

// COMMON CANDLE CALCULATIONS

// =====================

range = high - low

body = math.abs(close - open)

upperWick = high - math.max(open, close)

lowerWick = math.min(open, close) - low

totalWick = upperWick + lowerWick

// =====================

// BASE CANDLE LOGIC

// Body ≤ 50%, Wick ≥ 50%

// =====================

isBase = (range > 0) and (body <= 0.5 * range) and (totalWick >= 0.5 * range)

// =====================

// EXPLOSIVE GREEN CANDLE

// Body > 50%, Wick < 50%, Green

// =====================

isExplosiveGreen =

(range \> 0) and

(close \> open) and

(body \> 0.5 \* range) and

(totalWick \< 0.5 \* range)

// =====================

// STEP 2: LOOK LEFT + BELOW CMP

// Explosive Green → Base

// =====================

validSequence =

isBase and

isExplosiveGreen\[1\] and

high \< cmp and

high\[1\] \< cmp and

close \< cmp

// =====================

// STEP 3: DRAW DEMAND ZONE

// Proximal = Highest Body

// Distal = Lowest Wick

// =====================

if validSequence

proximal = close \> open ? close : open

distal   = low

box.new(bar_index, bar_index + 20, proximal, distal,

    bgcolor = color.new(color.green, 80),

    border_color = color.green)

Q: iPhone web app development in ASP.NET - where to begin? A:

Yes – Sitecore has mobile api access supported for Xamarin Forms Mobile app development. By using Sitecore’s Mobile SDK and Web API services, you can develop native cross-platform Xamarin apps, including iOS App Development and Android with access to Sitecore content. What you can use for developing a mobile app with Sitecore

Sitecore Mobile SDK for Xamarin

Mobile SDK for Sitecore provides, as part of its capabilities, a set of tools that aim  to assist developers in integrating Sitecore and Xamarin-based mobile applications. It’s available on NuGet, Xamarin Store and GitHub.

You can embed it directly into your Xamarin Forms project to develop X-platform apps in C#.

Useful links (Resources):

Sitecore Mobile SDK for Xamarin (Official Download & Docs) – Obtainable through the Sitecore Developer Portal.

Get the GitHub source of Sitecore Mobile SDK – contains sample code and implementations.

NuGet Packages: Both Standard and SSC versions.

Using Sitecore’s mobile API options means you don’t have to build custom backend services from scratch- you can reuse the same CMS content and workflows that power your website in your mobile apps. Combined with Xamarin Forms, this enables rapid mobile app development with shared C# code across platforms. enables rapid mobile app development with shared C# code across platforms.

Q: Capture images from RTSP stream A:

The challenge is photos stop saving after first 3 minutes (first 3 photos are taken in seconds but saved later during each minute). The solution is to ensure it saves every minute up to 24 hours.

import cv2
import time
import getpass
import numpy as np
import subprocess as sp
from datetime import datetime

imagesFolder = "C:/Users/" + getpass.getuser() + "/documents"

# RTSP Streaming:
in_stream = "rtsp://username:password@cameraIP/axis-media/media.amp"
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(in_stream)
frameRate = cap.get(5) #frame rate

# Get resolution of input video
width  = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH))
height = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))

# Release VideoCapture - it was used just for getting video resolution
cap.release()

in_stream = "rtsp://username:password@cameraIP/axis-media/media.amp"
FFMPEG_BIN = "ffmpeg.exe" # on Windows

# Suspecting camera supports TCP protocol hence added: '-rtsp_transport', 'tcp'
command = [ FFMPEG_BIN,
            '-rtsp_transport', 'tcp',
            '-i', in_stream,
            '-f', 'image2pipe',
            '-pix_fmt', 'bgr24',
            '-vcodec', 'rawvideo', '-an', '-']

# Open sub-process that gets in_stream as input and uses stdout as an output PIPE.
pipe = sp.Popen(command, stdout=sp.PIPE, bufsize=10**8)

cur_time = time.time()  # Get current time

# start_time_24h measures 24 hours
start_time_24h = cur_time

# start_time_1min measures 1 minute
start_time_1min = cur_time - 30  # Subtract 30 seconds for start grabbing first frame after 30 seconds (instead of waiting a minute for the first frame).

while True:
    # read width*height*3 bytes from stdout (= 1 frame)
    raw_frame = pipe.stdout.read(width*height*3)

    if len(raw_frame) != (width*height*3):
        print('Error reading frame!!!')  # Break the loop in case of an error (too few bytes were read).
        break

    cur_time = time.time()  # Get current time
    elapsed_time_1min = cur_time - start_time_1min  # Time elapsed from previous image saving.

    # If 60 seconds were passed, reset timer, and store image.
    if elapsed_time_1min >= 60:
        # Reset the timer that is used for measuring 60 seconds
        start_time_1min = cur_time

        # Transform the byte read into a numpy array, and reshape it to video frame dimensions
        frame = np.fromstring(raw_frame, np.uint8)
        frame = frame.reshape((height, width, 3))

        filename = imagesFolder + "/image_" + str(datetime.now().strftime("%d-%m-%Y_%I-%M-%S_%p"))  + ".jpg"
        #filename = "image_" + str(datetime.now().strftime("%d-%m-%Y_%I-%M-%S_%p"))  + ".jpg"
        cv2.imwrite(filename, frame)

        # Show frame for testing
        cv2.imshow('frame', frame)
        cv2.waitKey(1)

    elapsed_time_24h = time.time() - start_time_24h

    #Break loop after 24*60*60 seconds
    if elapsed_time_24h > 24*60*60:
        break

    #time.sleep(60 - elapsed_time) # Sleeping is a bad idea - we need to grab all the frames.

print ("Done!")
pipe.kill()  # Kill the sub-process after 24 hours
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
